results.name: Foam Roller Back
instructions: Sit on the floor with a foam roller behind you and lie back so it is under your upper back.
Support your head with your hands and lift your hips slightly.
Roll slowly up and down from the bottom of your shoulder blades to the top of your back.
Pause on tight spots and breathe.
tips: Don't roll your lower back directly.
Move slowly.
results.description: Foam Roller Back is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the upper back (back). Performed with a roller, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Middle Back.

results.name: Foam Roller Calves
instructions: Sit with your legs straight and a foam roller under your calves.
Lift your hips with your hands on the floor.
Roll slowly from your ankles to just below your knees.
Turn your legs in and out to reach the sides of your calves.
tips: Cross one leg over the other for more pressure.
Pause on tight spots.
results.description: Foam Roller Calves is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with a roller, it falls under the flexibility category.

results.name: Foam Roller Lateral Quads
instructions: Lie on your side with a foam roller under the outside of your thigh.
Support yourself on your forearm and your top foot.
Roll slowly between your hip and your knee.
Pause on tender areas and breathe, then switch sides.
tips: Take weight through your top foot if it is too intense.
Don't roll over your knee.
results.description: Foam Roller Lateral Quads is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a roller, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Abductors.

results.name: Foam Roller Quads
instructions: Lie face down with a foam roller under the front of your thighs.
Support yourself on your forearms.
Roll slowly from your hips to just above your knees.
Pause on tight spots and breathe.
tips: Roll one leg at a time for more pressure.
Keep your core tight.
results.description: Foam Roller Quads is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a roller, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors.

results.name: Forearms Pull With Opposite Hand Stretch
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder width apart and extend your right arm straight in front of your chest with your palm facing down.
Place your left hand over your right hand while keeping the working elbow straight and your shoulder relaxed.
Gently pull your right hand downward and toward your body until you feel a comfortable stretch along the top of your forearm.
Hold the stretch briefly, release your hand with control, and repeat for the desired duration before switching arms.
tips: Keep the elbow of your stretching arm fully extended throughout the movement.
Pull through the fingers rather than pressing directly against the wrist joint.
Stop if you feel sharp pain, tingling, or numbness in your wrist or hand.
Inhale before applying the stretch and exhale as you gently pull your fingers downward.
results.description: Forearms Pull With Opposite Hand Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the forearms (lower arms). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Shoulders.

results.name: Forearms Stretch on Wall Fingers Facing Down
instructions: Stand facing a wall and place the fingers of your right hand against it at shoulder height, pointing them downward. Keep your palm slightly away from the wall and maintain a small bend in your elbow.
Keep your fingers in contact with the wall as you slowly shift your body weight forward.
Gently press your right palm into the wall until you feel a comfortable stretch in your forearm.
Shift your weight backward and lift your palm away from the wall while keeping your fingers in contact, then repeat before switching to your left hand.
tips: Keep your fingers in contact with the wall throughout every repetition.
Maintain a small bend in your elbow instead of locking your arm.
Use a comfortable range of motion and stop if you feel pain, tingling, or numbness.
Inhale as you move your palm away and exhale as you press it into the wall.
results.description: Forearms Stretch on Wall Fingers Facing Down is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the forearms (lower arms). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Forearms, Biceps.

results.name: Forearms Stretch on Wall
instructions: Stand with your right side beside a wall and place your right palm flat against it at shoulder height.
Keep your right hand against the wall, with a bend in your elbow and your shoulder relaxed.
Slowly shift your weight forward until you feel a stretch along your right forearm.
Hold the stretch, then release and repeat with your left arm.
tips: Keep your palm and fingers flat against the wall.
Keep your stretching arm straight throughout the stretch.
Stop if you feel pain, tingling, or numbness.
Inhale before turning and exhale as you deepen the stretch.
results.description: Forearms Stretch on Wall is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the forearms (lower arms). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Chest, Shoulders.

results.name: Half Neck Rolls
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder width apart and cross your arms over your chest.
Lower your chin toward your chest and slowly roll your head from the left side toward the right side.
Reverse the movement and roll your head back toward the left, keeping your chin moving across the front of your chest.
Continue moving slowly from side to side for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your shoulders relaxed and away from your ears.
Do not roll your head backward or drop it behind your shoulders.
Stop if you feel pain, dizziness, or tingling.
Inhale as you reach one side and exhale as your chin moves across your chest.
results.description: Half Neck Rolls is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the levator scapulae (neck). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

results.name: Hands Clapped Forearms Stretch
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder width apart and press your palms together in front of your chest with your fingers pointing upward.
Keep your palms together and your elbows lifted as you rotate your hands until your fingers point downward.
Gently lower your joined hands toward your abdomen until you feel a stretch through your wrists and forearms.
Reverse the movement, return your fingers upward, then lower your arms to the starting position.
tips: Rotate your hands slowly without separating them.
Lower your hands only as far as your wrists remain comfortable.
Stop if you feel pain, tingling, or numbness.
Inhale as your fingers point upward and exhale as you lower your hands.
results.description: Hands Clapped Forearms Stretch is an advanced single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the forearms (lower arms). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Shoulders.

results.name: Kneeling Forearm Flexor Stretch
instructions: Kneel on the floor and place your palms on the floor with your fingers pointing back toward your knees.
Keep your arms straight.
Gently sit back until you feel a stretch along the inside of your forearms.
Hold, breathing steadily, then release.
tips: Go gently; wrists are sensitive.
Keep your palms flat.
results.description: Kneeling Forearm Flexor Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the forearms (lower arms). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category.
